business_scope.primary_industry_name: Visual Web Template and Low-Code Web Application Builder

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar), ss 5–13 (incorporation), s 41 (articles of association), s 160–170 (registered office and registers); Companies (Fees) Regulations 2015; Beneficial Ownership (Electronic Records) Regulations 2018; Income Tax Act 2010, s 6 (residence) as applied to exempt-company elections.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, 200 Town Range, Gibraltar GX11 1AA; online filing via the COMPASS e-filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation (Form CO-1) together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association; final issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation under s 13 of the Companies Act 2014.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a private company limited by shares; the memorandum must state its authorised capital and the statement of capital may reflect one subscriber share of GBP 1.00 issued at par. No escrow account or capital deposit is required for a Gibraltar-incorporated exempt-company structure.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Incorporation Application, Memorandum and Articles of Association filed with the Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar, be and are hereby approved. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Company be fixed at [Registered Office Address], Gibraltar, and that the Registers of Members, Directors and Charges be kept there. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] be appointed Director and [Name] Company Secretary until the next Annual General Meeting. RESOLVED FURTHER that the allotment of one Ordinary Share of GBP 1.00 to the subscriber be confirmed, and the Directors be authorized to open bank and payment-rail accounts and execute all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar (COMPASS e-filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name clearance request via the COMPASS portal or at the Companies House counter. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company and cannot contain prohibited terms under the Companies Act 2014. Upon clearance, the name is reserved for 28 days pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: Letter of authority from the intended shareholder or formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, re-file with an alternative proposed name or supply the written consent of the existing name holder; the first re-submission is free of charge and must occur within the 28-day reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarization of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Notary Public and licensed formation agent regulated by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association with an objects clause permitting software development, SaaS delivery, and low-code platform services; execute the subscriber pages before a Gibraltar notary and arrange apostille certification where execution occurs overseas; obtain signed consents of the first director and company secretary.
required_dossiers: Form CO-2 consent of first directors and company secretary
Subscriber passport copies and proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is rejected for defective execution, re-execute before a Gibraltar-qualified notary; if the Registrar queries the objects clause, file a supplementary memorandum by way of a corrective submission within the 14-day query window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of incorporation application to the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar (COMPASS portal or counter service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form CO-1 together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, statutory consents, statement of capital, and registered office consent. Obtain a date-stamped filing receipt. The Registrar examines the application against the formal requirements of the Companies Act 2014.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Form CO-2 consent of directors and secretary
Statement of capital and initial share allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any Registrar query within 14 days by filing corrected documents; a formal refusal is appealable to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar under s 13(4) of the Companies Act 2014.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar and HM Government of Gibraltar Treasury
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Settle the incorporation fee of GBP 250 (USD 320 equivalent) by card or bank transfer; obtain the official receipt. Confirm that no capital or stamp duty is exigible on nominal share capital under the Stamp Duties (Gibraltar) legislative framework.
required_dossiers: Proof of bank transfer or card authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Incorrect tariff payments are adjusted by written application to the Treasury; any underpayment must be cured within 5 business days to avoid a late-payment penalty; overpayments are refunded within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon substantive review, the Registrar enters the company on the commercial register and issues the Certificate of Incorporation showing the company number, legal name, and date of incorporation under s 13(1) of the Companies Act 2014. The company comes into existence on the certificate date.
required_dossiers: Complete registered particulars extracted from the application file
Certified copy of the approved Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Clerical errors in the certificate are corrected by an administrative correction request (Form CO-6) filed within 21 days; no court process or reincorporation is required for ministerial mistakes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Gibraltar tax registration and exempt-company status confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (Director of Income Tax)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Gibraltar reference number and submit the exempt-company election confirming that management and control are outside Gibraltar, such that foreign-source income falls outside the charge to tax under the Income Tax Act 2010. Maintain a written management-and-control file evidencing board meetings and decision-making location.
required_dossiers: Directors' details and beneficial ownership statement
Business description covering ISIC 6201 no-code software builder operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax residency is disputed, tender the management-and-control evidence and request an advanced ruling under s 7 of the Income Tax Act 2010; any adverse determination is appealable to the Income Tax Tribunal within 45 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered office and statutory registers compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar through a licensed Gibraltar registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the statutory seat at the approved Gibraltar registered office; open and keep the register of members, register of directors and secretaries, and register of charges; file persons with significant control particulars in the central beneficial ownership register within 30 days of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Non-compliance with register-keeping attracts penalties up to GBP 500; remedy by voluntary corrective filing within 30 days, accompanied by an explanatory note, to avoid strike-off proceedings under s 170 of the Companies Act 2014.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking and payment-rail account mandate (Stripe Billing and Paddle onboarding)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GFSC-licensed Gibraltar bank or passported e-money institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete corporate account onboarding for payment processing; present the bank mandate resolution; provide beneficial ownership declarations and economic substance confirmation; complete AML/KYC interviews for directors and qualifying shareholders; integrate Stripe Billing and Paddle using the Certificate of Incorporation and the first board resolution.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank mandate extract of the first board resolution
Passports and proof of address for directors and 25%+ shareholders
SaaS business plan for the no-code website builder (ISIC 6201)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: An AML-oriented refusal may be cured by enhanced due-diligence evidence such as bank references and source-of-funds statements; if still declined, apply to an alternate GFSC-licensed EMI, and for discriminatory treatment submit a complaint to the GFSC.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None applicable — ISIC 6201 software and low-code platform development is not an industrial licensed activity in Gibraltar; the coordinating economic facilitation body is the Gibraltar Development and Enterprise Agency (GDEA).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industry operating licence is required; the company may lawfully commence business upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation and tax registration. Any physical office fit-out remains subject to ordinary building-consent conditions under the Town and Country Planning Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change, HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C — exempt from a full EIA; office-only software operations do not meet Schedule 1 or Schedule 2 thresholds under the Town and Country Planning (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 2018.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, combustion, or VOC thresholds apply to code-based software production. Compliance obligations are limited to: WEEE disposal under the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (Gibraltar) Regulations; battery and UPS handling under the Hazardous Waste (Gibraltar) Regulations; and a server-room ambient-noise limit of 40 dB(A) at the nearest noise-sensitive receptor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and means-of-escape certification from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service is required before building occupancy; structural load approval and electrical inspection certification from Building Control, Development and Planning Service, apply to any server room; employers' liability insurance and a low-risk workplace risk assessment are required under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act (Gibraltar), together with an NICEIC electrical installation certificate for office and IT equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (administration of income tax and GIBVAT); online filing via the Government of Gibraltar taxation portal (gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation). HMRC (UK) has no income tax or VAT jurisdiction in Gibraltar; however, for customs purposes Gibraltar is part of the UK customs territory under the Taxation (Cross-border Trade) Act 2018 as applied by the Customs (Gibraltar) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019. The Bermuda Registrar of Companies administers no income tax but receives economic substance filings under the Bermuda Economic Substance Amendment Act 2018.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: register the Bermuda Exempted Company as an external company with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 2014 if it establishes a place of business in Gibraltar; obtain the Gibraltar company registration number. Step 2: apply to the Income Tax Office for the Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN) before commencing chargeable activity; a foreign-incorporated company becomes Gibraltar tax-resident if central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar. Step 3: register as an employer for tax-deduction (PAYE-equivalent) withholding and social insurance if staff are engaged in Gibraltar. Step 4: register for GIBVAT only if taxable non-zero-rated turnover exceeds the statutory threshold (see indirect tax nexus). Step 5: file the Bermuda economic substance notification/declaration with the Bermuda Registrar of Companies and, if Gibraltar tax-resident, comply with the Gibraltar Economic Substance (Companies and Limited Partnerships) Act 2020 notification requirements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: the Bermuda Exempted Company enjoys exemption from Bermuda income, capital gains, dividend and withholding taxes under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 (exemption assurance to 2035), and Bermuda levies no indirect tax. The Tax_Exempt_Zone classification is preserved only while the company is not managed and controlled in Gibraltar; a Gibraltar tax-resident company is subject to entity-level Gibraltar corporation tax at 12.5% on worldwide profits under the Income Tax Act 2010, as amended, with the former 0% qualifying-company regime abolished in 2010.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US check-the-box election is available because the Bermuda Exempted Company is a per se corporation under US Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-2(b)(8). Gibraltar allows no election to opt out of corporation tax; a foreign-incorporated company may align its residence by ensuring that central management and control is, or is not, exercised in Gibraltar (Income Tax Act 2010). Gibraltar has adopted hybrid mismatch rules aligned with OECD BEPS Action 2 and ATAD, but no check-the-box or hybrid instrument election is available or relevant to this standard ISIC 6201 no-code website-builder structure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary authority for sterling); in Gibraltar, the Financial Services Commission (GFSC) is the banking and financial regulator, and the Government of Gibraltar (Ministry of Finance) administers local currency issuance and national exchange-control formalities under the Gibraltar Currency Notes Act 1934 and Exchange Control Act 1972.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar maintains a hard peg of the Gibraltar pound (GIP) to pound sterling (GBP) at par. There are no exchange controls restricting current or capital account transactions; profit remittances are freely permitted for companies holding a Gibraltar tax-exempt certificate (ETA) provided they satisfy the Economic Substance regulations. For a Bermuda Exempted Company not tax-resident in Gibraltar, distributions to shareholders are generally not subject to Gibraltar withholding tax, but cross-border payments must be supported by substance and beneficial ownership register filings to avoid classification as passive fund movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Gibraltar does not, as a British Overseas Territory, require export proceeds to be surrendered to a central authority. There is no mandatory conversion quota or statutory timeline. Export receipts may be credited to any segregated account in foreign currency and used freely for operational disbursements, subject to AML record-keeping and documentary evidence of the underlying delivery of services.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility through UK-regulated electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Revolut Business, and Bunq, which accept Gibraltar-incorporated companies as low-risk clients via remote onboarding; medium feasibility through EEA EMIs due to reduced SEPA passporting protections in Gibraltar. Legal constraints require the EMI to hold adequate e-money licenses, apply FATF-compliant KYC, and in some cases place limits on Bermuda-incorporated shareholders. A Gibraltar-registered branch office or local substance provider materially increases EMI approval rates.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally accepted for low-risk, non-resident exempt companies if the UBOs and directors pass fully digitized identity verification and video interviews. Practically, Gibraltar-licensed banks often require at least one director or the local agent to attend in person at the bank's Gibraltar office to authenticate original passports, board resolutions, and powers of attorney. A notarized certified copy set plus apostille is mandatory for remote jurisdictions such as Bermuda.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore-exempt company incorporated in a zero-tax jurisdiction (Bermuda) without visible commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, ETA/tax exemption certificate (if obtained), audited financials, business plan, and evidence of an active UK/Gibraltar-facing website and software platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda-Gibraltar nexus indicates possible tax evasion or shell activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare inter-group legal agreements illustrating the Bermuda company as the global IP holder and the Gibraltar entity as an operational/banking servicing arm; submit organizational chart, board minutes, services agreements, transfer-pricing documentation, and tax residence certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-speed online payment activity via Stripe or Paddle may portend unauthorized third-party transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver platform privacy policy, merchant services agreements, transaction monitoring reports, complaint handling procedures, and historical bank statements proving consistent revenue source.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound funding of a Gibraltar treasury requires SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the parent/Bermuda account, using a GIP/GBP or USD purpose code such as 'Capital / contribution to working capital', 'Intercompany funding', or 'Shareholder loan'. Supporting verification must include (i) an inbound remittance letter from the beneficiary bank, (ii) the underlying board resolution authorizing the capital placement or loan, (iii) the duly executed facility agreement, and (iv) the beneficial ownership register and tax-residence evidence. Funds should land in a designated Capital Escrow Account or segregated operational account to allow clearing and reconciliation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing is executed through SWIFT MT103 for general disbursements, MT202 COV for interbank transfers, and optionally a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) for contractual services procurement. For no-code platform disbursements, preferred rails are SWIFT MT103, SEPA CT (where the counterparty is an EEA bank), and Faster Payments-style accounts where available; all outbound transfers require dual-approval, invoice copies, tax input slips, and proof of economic substance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry, H.M. Government of Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 21 days after the annual review date; generally the anniversary of registration in Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty GBP 150; continued default accrues daily penalties and the Registrar may apply for strike-off of the Gibraltar registration after 3 months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation (submitted with Form OCR-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registry of Companies (Beneficial Ownership Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the review date; any change in beneficial ownership must also be reported within 14 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Conviction carries a fine up to GBP 10,000 and up to 2 years' imprisonment for the responsible officer; ongoing breach extends to daily default fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements or Audit Exemption Notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 13 months after the previous financial year end; if audit-exempt, a signed exemption statement may be lodged together with the OCR-1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late delivery penalty up to GBP 5,000; persistent default may result in administrative strike-off and disqualification of the local authorised representative.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is triggered only where the Gibraltar branch of the Bermuda exempted company exceeds two of the following three thresholds in a financial year: turnover GIP 10.2M, gross assets GIP 5.1M, average number of employees 50. A typical low-code SaaS platform with no physical branch and low Gibraltar-source revenue remains audit-exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 and Gibraltar GAAP; IFRS as adopted for use in Gibraltar is mandatory for large overseas companies. A Bermuda-incorporated exempted company may file its Bermuda financial statements if prepared under IFRS or US GAAP and accompanied by a reconciliation to Gibraltar requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Gibraltar registered office must maintain and annually confirm a register of beneficial owners identifying any person with more than 25% equity, voting, or management control. Shareholding transfers and buybacks executed by the Bermuda parent must be reported to the local authorised representative within 14 days, followed by a signed update to the Gibraltar UBO sub-register.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 8,500 for audit-exempt compilation review; USD 12,000 - 25,000 for a full statutory audit if thresholds are exceeded

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 10% flat corporate income tax on chargeable income accruing in or derived from Gibraltar (Income Tax Act 2010, s.8); the Bermuda domicile of the exempted company imposes a 0% corporate income tax rate at the sovereign level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential IP boxes remain available; the former exemption for passive interest and royalties was annulled as unlawful State Aid (Case T-211/14 RENV) and replaced with taxable treatment at the flat 10% rate. Effective rate is zero only where the Bermuda Exempted Company is managed and controlled outside Gibraltar and derives no Gibraltar-source income, because Gibraltar applies a territorial charging basis. Capital allowances are available for computer equipment and software. Trading losses may be carried forward indefinitely under s.37 ITaA 2010; the pipeline schema intentionally encodes a conventional 5-year model cap for cross-jurisdiction comparability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Corporation Tax Return (Company Return), filed through the Gibraltar Income Tax Office e-Filing Portal (Gibraltar Tax e-Services, www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation); the return must be accompanied by the statutory financial statements, the tax computation, and, where applicable, the Economic Substance (ESR) return and transfer-pricing disclosure.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual on a preceding-year basis; the tax year of assessment is the calendar year and the chargeable income is the profit of the accounting period that ended in the preceding year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return due within 9 months of the accounting period end (i.e., 30 September for a 31 December year-end) unless the Commissioner's return notice under s.41 Income Tax Act 2010 prescribes a different date; the tax assessed is payable within 30 days of the notice of assessment, with interim payments on account collectable where the prior-year charge exceeds the de minimis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name, company number, Gibraltar tax reference, registered office, and entity type (Bermuda Exempted Company registered as an overseas company in Gibraltar).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the overseas-company identification block; attach the Bermuda certificate of incorporation and the Gibraltar overseas-company registration certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the accounting period (typically 1 January to 31 December).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the Gibraltar return to the audited Bermuda accounting period; any change of accounting date must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total reportable turnover from the no-code website builder platform (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210): subscription fees, usage fees, one-time build fees, and platform settlements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose gross sales settled through Stripe_Billing and Paddle even if the merchant-of-record is a foreign affiliate; apply Gibraltar source rules and exclude non-Gibraltar-source turnover only with contemporaneous evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs: cloud hosting, payment-processing commissions, and third-party design-asset and infrastructure licences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach merchant-of-record statements; non-residents may deduct only costs attributable to Gibraltar-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 3 minus Box 4 computed under Gibraltar-recognised accounting standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Return nil for a fully non-resident exempted company without Gibraltar-source revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payroll, subcontractors, online advertising, software tools, legal and accounting fees, bank charges, and travel.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses incurred in producing Gibraltar chargeable income are deductible; head-office costs and intercompany fees require arm's-length benchmarking.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation-equivalent allowances for computer equipment, servers, software, and development-related plant and machinery.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only assets used in the taxable Gibraltar activity; apportion on a time-and-use basis where mixed use occurs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source turnover and passive income excluded under Gibraltar's territorial charging provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all exempt income and retain evidence of source (server location, contracting counterparty, place of economic performance) to withstand an BEPS/ESR challenge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back or deduction reflecting arm's-length pricing on controlled transactions, including management fees, IP royalties, and intercompany SaaS licensing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with Gibraltar intercompany arrangements must append a transfer-pricing Local File and benchmark study.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Trading losses brought forward and set off against current-year chargeable profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses computed under Gibraltar rules may be carried forward; Bermuda-exempt accounting losses are not automatically deductible in Gibraltar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net chargeable income multiplied by the 10% flat rate; deduct interim payments, credits, and unilateral relief; state net tax payable or repayable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nil charge where no Gibraltar-source income arises; file nonetheless to obtain a nil assessment and preserve the statutory limitation period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director declarations, audit opinion summary, ESR relevant-activity notification (Y/N), and beneficial-ownership register reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Bermuda exempted company earning IP income must complete the Gibraltar Economic Substance declaration and annex the substance report.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers an automatic penalty of GBP 300 plus a daily surcharge of up to GBP 60; inaccurate returns attract a penalty of up to 100% of the tax undercharged, reducible for prompted voluntary disclosure; fraudulent returns are prosecuted criminally with an unlimited fine and imprisonment of up to 7 years; late payments bear statutory interest from the due date.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Gibraltar imposes no withholding tax on dividends paid by Gibraltar-resident companies to any shareholder, including the Bermuda parent and other non-resident recipients; there is no domestic dividend WHT legislation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No treaty relief is needed for dividends because the statutory WHT is nil. For deductible interest and royalty payments, the Gibraltar payer must hold the recipient's Gibraltar Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), issued by the Commissioner of Income Tax on Form TRC/G, together with a Bermuda tax-residence declaration and a beneficial-ownership statement; the UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation Agreement (2019) and the Bermuda-Gibraltar administrative arrangements require the TRC to be submitted with the annual return to sustain the deduction and to access any treaty rate should a future WHT be introduced.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 0% withholding tax on outbound interest and royalties paid to non-residents; however, the payer's deduction is disallowed where the recipient lacks beneficial-ownership and TRC evidence. Treaty reference (UK-Gibraltar DTA 2019): 0% on dividends, 0% on interest, and 0% on software/IP royalties at arm's-length amounts, with application through the standard TRC-based claim process.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: required where aggregate controlled transactions exceed GBP 1,000,000 per annum (GIP pegged 1:1 to sterling); Master File: required where Gibraltar group turnover exceeds GBP 50,000,000; all controlled transactions below the threshold must still be supported by contemporaneous arm's-length evidence on demand.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance (Companies and Partnerships) Act 2019 (ESR) governs. The no-code website-builder business that owns or licenses software IP is an 'Intellectual Property Business' relevant activity, requiring: (i) core income-generating activities performed in Gibraltar (development supervision, licensing, versioning, support); (ii) adequate qualified employees, premises, and expenditure proportionate to the IP; (iii) annual ESR filing alongside the tax return; and (iv) board minutes evidencing management and control in Gibraltar. A Bermuda exempted company that is only paper-registered in Gibraltar, or that manages its IP from the UK, fails the substance test; conversely, an entity wholly managed and controlled in Bermuda with no Gibraltar-source activity has no Gibraltar tax or ESR exposure. The Tax-Exempt-Zone classification does not displace ESR obligations where any Gibraltar-source IP income is earned.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Stripe_Billing or Paddle SaaS receipts, filing false revenue schedules, or claiming Bermuda exempt status while exercising full management and control from a Gibraltar office (de facto migration).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the full tax evaded plus penalties up to 100% of the undercharge with aggravated rates for concealment; criminal prosecution for fraudulent evasion of income tax with an unlimited fine and imprisonment up to 7 years; asset-freezing orders, income-netting orders, and restitution of evaded sums with statutory interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who knowingly participate in or by neglect permit the offence are personally prosecuted; courts may issue travel bans and passport-surrender orders during confiscation proceedings, impose personal restitution orders, and disqualify directors for up to 15 years under the Gibraltar Companies Act.
